summary: I built the shared REFERENCE page (ts/src/cmp/ReadmeRef.ts) for ts, go, py and c, and then zig, in a copy of the v2 clone. Every heading and sentence is written once and conditioned on an extended SdkDescription. Each provider supplies one declared RefFacts table (signatures, a closed set of member kinds, null literal, key layout) plus three printers (type, key, instance). Operation examples and the feature snippet go through the existing example representation. ReadmeRef_ts/go/py/c/zig are deleted. Across 21 model variations (two new ones, ref-issues and no-test, expose the catalogued defects), every changed line in the five languages has a stated reason: 0 UNEXPLAINED. The 15 unported languages are byte-identical apart from two fixes I made in the already-shared ReadmeRefFeatures (the escaped-backtick leak and S09), and the README sections ported in v2 are unchanged (diff2: 0 unexplained, 0 outside). Lanes at HEAD: ts README 16/16, go README 12/12, py README with real pytest 12/12, c DOC 6/6 (6/6 again at the final HEAD). My first run failed ts 5/16 and py 3/12 for one reason, an action example that no test mode can run. I dropped that example: the table names the operation and the route, and the issue is not intrinsic to the approach. Suite without toolchain lanes: 2534 tests, 2528 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped. I extended the runtime-facts guard so that every declared reference signature must exist in the runtime, and every stream/client/entopts/options/utility/make/name member the runtime defines must be declared; a negative control fails as it should. H2 holds for this page: five languages go from 2,196 to 967 lines (2.27x; 1.92x non-blank non-comment), and the projection to 20 is 4.86x with measured-size providers and 3.07x if they are twice that size. Both sections together project to 2.74x, or 2.03x if the remaining providers are 1.5x the measured size. Of the catalogued issues, 17 checks are fixed by shared code in all five languages (issuecheck.js). N11 (the js fence) and the perl `{id}` defect need the js and perl ports. Negatives: a few true language-specific facts were lost (zig's StreamResult `throw:false` clause, ts tester's Returns line, py's `# str` type comments in create examples, ts's update comment). clojure is not ported: its client has no type name for the shared h2. Neither zig nor clojure has a toolchain here.
stopped_at: Finished in the brief's order of importance. Done: 1 and 2 for ts and go, then py and c (description, shared page, providers, retired components); 3 (provider facts, the extended guard and its negative control); 4 (mdCell/mdInline); 5 (ReadmeRef_ts/go/py/c/zig deleted, unported byte-identical); 6 (issue checks on variations); 7 (prose, code blocks, source lines, purity); 8 (build, suite, golden, the ts/go/py/c lanes at HEAD); 9 (PORTING.md); and zig. NOT done: (a) clojure's reference port. Its client has no class (old h2 '## Client', '### make-sdk'), and the shared h2 prints layout.client ('api'), so it needs a fact or a layout field first. (b) zig output was not compiled (command -v zig: missing); its test is the reasoned diff, 0 unexplained. (c) Feature defaults are not in DescRef. ReadmeRefFeatures (shared) still reads featureDocs from the model itself. (d) The guard does not check the collection noun, recordType, nullValue, errVar, ok/err, maps, container, valueType, body.values or direct ctrl. (e) I did not re-run the upgrade walk or the lifecycle suites on this build. (f) No timings. (g) The OLD lane numbers are from stage 1 and v2's runs, not re-run here.

names: Names reach the description only through the v2 Naming hook (cmp/<lang>/Naming_<lang>.ts, found by optionalComponent(ctx$, target, 'Naming') in describeTarget). The reference page adds one name source: DescEntity.className = entityClassName(e, entityCollection(model)), computed in sdkdesc.ts describe(). It is the same function the code generators use for the class (zig Entity_zig.ts:24 `const cls = entityClassName(entity, entityColl)`; ts and py fragments use EntyClass from the same helper). That is how U34 shows PlanetEntityClient in ref-issues. Signatures hold tokens ({sdk} {client} {ctor} {module} {accessor} {var} {Class} {Name}), which the shared fill() in ReadmeRef.ts substitutes from desc.layout and DescEntity; providers do no string work on a name. Per language, one function called by both the code generator and the description: ts packageName (Package_ts.ts:68, Naming_ts.ts:11); go goModule (Main_go.ts:48, Naming_go.ts:13); py pyPackageDir (Main_py.ts:49, Naming_py.ts:13); c cIdent/cVarName (MainEntity_c.ts:16-17, Naming_c.ts:14-20; EntityBase_c.ts:47 names the stream function `${evar}_stream`, which the c facts mirror as '{var}_stream'); zig zigVarName (MainEntity_zig.ts:21, Naming_zig.ts:15). Field types come from canonToType(t, '<literal language>') in each provider's ref.type, never from target.name, so the go~go2 alias prints go types (N04/U06/M04, shown on alias-go2).

provider_purity: node harness/purity.js counts per provider. Model reads: 0 in ts, go, py, c and zig. Naming rules: 0. Operation names outside the facts table: 0. The import check flags canonToType in all five and canonKey in c. These are shared pure maps from a canonical sentinel to a type name, called with the provider's own literal language: the type-name table stage 1 classed as syntax, now in one place. I count them as allowed, which takes the strict count from 6 to 1. The one remaining hit is `case 'item': return r.entity.sym.vars + '[i]'` in Syntax_c. That is a C index expression, not a naming rule, and v2 had it too: running purity.js on the v2 clone gives 1, although v2 reported 0. What a script cannot see: the RefFacts tables are hand-written data. The runtimefacts guard re-derives the signatures and the presence of seven member kinds from the fragments, templates and Main/MainEntity/EntityBase components, but not the nouns (collection, maps, container, valueType) or the body phrase. Those can still be false. Provider-declared English phrases remain in body.values and body.once (e.g. 'a `Buffer`, ... stream or string'), counted as declared-fact words.
migration: Nothing new merged; the v2 lifecycle change (migrate's a49fddc0/7bb5161b/c193a603 as 1fcc1ef5/9481257f/61e8b338) is in the base. ReadmeRef follows the same rule as ReadmeQuick: loadOptional(`./cmp/<t>/ReadmeRef_<t>`) wins over the provider, so a pack or a project override keeps its page, and the record-gated retire/prune in target.ts and doctor.ts applies to a leftover ReadmeRef_<lang> exactly as it does to ReadmeQuick_<lang>. The suite's retire.test passes within the 2534-test run. I did NOT re-run the upgrade walk (v2/mig) or the lifecycle rows on this build; that is a gap. The golden manifest (test/golden/add-output.txt) was refreshed twice, and records ReadmeRef_ts/go/py/c/zig as no longer shipped.

tests: Changed or added in the clone: ts/test/runtimefacts.test.ts adds a test per provider, 'the declared reference members are what its runtime defines'. Every declared signature (client, entity, test constructors, ops) must name a function defined in the runtime fragments, templates or Main/MainEntity/EntityBase components. Every member the runtime defines among stream, client, entopts, options, utility, make and name must be declared. It skips providers without ref. ts/test/media.test.ts selects targets with a ReadmeRef_<t> or a Syntax_<t>. ts/test/golden/add-output.txt was refreshed. The two new harness variations (ref-issues, no-test) serve as fixtures for the issue checks, but they are harness-only, not suite tests. Run: the full suite (2534 tests, 0 fail), the four documentation lanes, and the negative control above.
gaps: clojure's reference port is not done: its client has no type, and the shared h2 '## {layout.client}' would print '## api'. It needs a fact (for example a client heading) or a layout field.
zig output was not compiled (no zig here); the test is the reasoned diff only.
Feature defaults are not in DescRef: ReadmeRefFeatures (shared) still reads featureDocs from the model.
The guard does not check RuntimeFacts.collection, recordType, nullValue, errVar, errSlot, ok/err, nor RefFacts.maps, container, valueType, body.values or none against the runtime.

Lost facts: zig StreamResult's throw:false clause; ts tester's 'Returns: DemoSDK instance in test mode' and the accessor parameter table; py's '# str' comments in create examples; ts's '// Fields to update' comment; go's GetName print.
Actions have no example: no test mode can run one and the payload is not in the model, so the table names the operation and route only.

D26 is only partly fixed: optspec has no descriptions, so the row text is held once in sdkdesc.ts; ReadmeModel/ReadmeOptions tables were not touched, so the README options table still disagrees with the REFERENCE rows (brief2 item 8 remains for those sections).
The OLD lane numbers were not re-run here (taken from stage 1 and v2).
The upgrade walk and the lifecycle rows were not re-run on this build.

The issue checks for the unported contrast columns (js, java, perl) use loose regexes and are indicative only; S13 for java/perl reads '--' because the check's heading regex does not match those pages.
The diffref.js reason rules are context rules (by section and heading), not per-line rules; some are broad (the Common-members rule tags 2,553 lines).
The 'both sections' after-count leaves out ReadmeTop's shared quick-start hook (about 54 lines).
surprises: The examples needed no new provider printer. refOpBlock reuses the quick-start statements (attempt, call, each, print), and the feature snippet is a client statement. Stage 1's proposed opExample/actionCall/featureActivation provider members were unnecessary.

The action example cannot be made runnable in any language: test modes reject an unknown action ('Operation "create" action "terraform" is not valid'), and ts requires the create fields. The old ts page escaped this only because its comment made it an 'illustration'. My first lane run caught it (ts 5 and py 3 failures).
The test constructors exist in every runtime whether or not the test feature ships (Main.fragment.ts:325, py :354, go :390, c :346). S13 is about a false sentence, not a missing method.
c also reads fetchargs ctrl (Main.fragment.c:90) and defines `<evar>_stream` (EntityBase_c.ts:47). Stage 1 named only py for ctrl and did not check c for stream. zig also reads ctrl.

Stage 1 section 5 was wrong or incomplete in places. optspec holds no descriptions, so 'option rows from optspec' gives keys and types but not text. The proposed clientTypeName/entityTypeName provider functions were replaced by the naming hook plus one `classes` boolean. c's '(list)/(map)' type annotation and its options container type ('voxgig_value*' vs 'map') needed two facts, not one. An `options()`/`utility()` absence in c is correct, as the runtime has none.

Sharing the shared ReadmeRefFeatures fixes changed 2,280 lines in the 15 unported languages. That is the proposal working as intended, but it means 'unported byte-identical' can only hold up to fixes to already-shared code.
v2's purity report of 0 was 1 by its own script (the c index expression).

hypotheses.evidence: REFERENCE for five languages (ts go py c zig): 0 model reads and 0 naming rules in providers (purity.js). 0 sentences written in providers, and declared-fact words are 0.1-0.9% of prose words (proseref.js), far under 15%. Breaking interface changes since stage 1's first commit: about 6 in all (block->before, RuntimeWords->RuntimeFacts, Ent.sym, Expr 'fields', builders taking facts, RefFacts.container), under the ~10 line. Both sections together across 20: 2.74x, or 2.03x with 1.5x providers. This depends on the reference reusing the description, representation and quick-start printers, which it did: +378 infrastructure lines and about 50 per language. The quick start alone remains refuted (v2: 1.59-1.66x), so H2 holds only for the pair of sections.

Of the 21 catalogued REFERENCE issues plus the uncatalogued ones, every one applicable to the five ported languages is fixed by shared code (issuecheck.js, OLD X / NEW - on the exposing variation). The N04 family needs a one-line per-language fact (the literal language in ref.type), N11 needs the js port, and stream is fixed by each provider declaring its member, enforced by the new guard. Per-language edits are about 3 of 25, around the 10% line, and each is a declared fact rather than a correction.

handoff:
Files. Shared page: ts/src/cmp/ReadmeRef.ts (refText, memberText, fill, keyTable, constructorText, testText, instanceText, entityText, featuresText). Description: ts/src/helpers/sdkdesc.ts (describeRef, describeEntity, describeOp, OPTION_TEXT). Representation and provider interface: ts/src/helpers/example.ts (RefFacts, RefSyntax, MemberKind, refOpBlock, featureBlock). Sentences per result style: ts/src/helpers/runtimeprose.ts (opText, failsSentence). Escaping: ts/src/helpers/markdown.ts. Body note facts: ts/src/helpers/media.ts. Feature reference (already shared): ts/src/cmp/ReadmeRefFeatures.ts. Providers: ts/project/.sdk/src/cmp/{ts,go,py,c,zig}/Syntax_<lang>.ts. Guard: ts/test/runtimefacts.test.ts.

The porting guide for the fourteen remaining languages is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f1977c62-4748-5872-8f72-6f448dbac3f1/scratchpad/design/proto2/ref/PORTING.md (205 lines). In brief:
(1) What a language writes, in order. Naming_<lang> first, calling the code generator's own naming functions (extract one into utility_<lang> if the generator inlines it). Then RuntimeFacts: pick a ResultStyle, and add a style plus its sentences in runtimeprose.ts and its STYLE check if none is true (swift Value/asNative, rust Result, perl die). Then the quick-start printers (client, call, each, print, attempt, comment, expr; before for hoisting; program only if the README test RUNS whole programs). Then RefFacts, every value read off the runtime: classes, noun, none, keys, maps, container, valueType, ctor, test[], accessor, op sigs with {Class}, client/entity Members of the closed MemberKind set in page order, direct.returns/signal, prepare.returns/fails, body, cancel. Then ref.type = canonToType(t, '<literal lang>'), ref.key, ref.instance. Then delete ReadmeQuick_/ReadmeTopQuick_/ReadmeRef_<lang>.
(2) How to check: npm run build, runtimefacts/optional/media tests, npm run golden, then gen.js new, diff2.js, diffref.js with PORTED extended, issuecheck.js, purity.js, proseref.js, metrics3.js, the suite, and the language's README_LANES or DOC_LANES lane (command -v the compiler first).
(3) Rules. No model, ctx$ or utility import in a provider; names only from desc.layout and Ent.sym; no op names outside the facts table; no sentences; no whether-decisions; every declared signature defined by the runtime and every defined member declared.
(4) Reporting. If the interface cannot express something, stop and record the construct, the file:line, the smallest change, breaking or additive, and the providers it forces.
(5) Traps. A new Expr/Stmt kind breaks every switch. Regenerate before diffing. Never rebuild while a run is going. members() inlines maps below depth 0. Data ops always take data. A REFERENCE block gets a fresh Scope. There is no action example. Test constructors exist without the feature. js fences js. lean keeps its own component. ocaml's 'Fields' and clojure's 'Members' are not in the noun union.
(6) clojure needs a client-heading fact first.

For whoever builds on this: the next step that pays most is porting the README options table and entity sections to the same description (desc.ref.optionRows already exists), so the ts README stops contradicting its own REFERENCE (brief2 item 8). After that, extend the guard to the nouns and phrases it cannot yet check.
